features.title: Wino Assistant
features.description: Press a shortcut in any app, then type or say what you want done: find, move, reply or delete, even several steps in one sentence. Wino shows its plan and changes nothing until you say Yes. Part of Wino Intelligence, in Settings > Wino Assistant.

features.title: Exchange Server and IMAP secure sign-in
features.description: Bring your work account to Wino: add your organization's Exchange Server for mail, calendar, contacts and To Do. IMAP accounts can now sign in securely in your browser, with no app password. Just type your email address and Wino finds the rest.

features.title: Privacy & security settings
features.description: Keep senders from knowing when you read their mail. Block trackers or all remote content, set rules for senders and domains, clean tracking from links, and get a warning before risky attachments open. Find it in Settings > Mail > Privacy & security.

features.title: App lock
features.description: Keep Wino Mail private on a shared PC. Lock it with Windows Hello or a PIN of its own, and it asks each time you open the window. Mail keeps syncing while it's locked, and notifications can stay read-only. Turn it on in Settings > General > App lock.

features.title: Account groups
features.description: Linked inboxes are now account groups. Give each group a name, a color and an icon, then choose whether its folders are combined into one inbox or each account keeps its own. Create them in Settings > Manage accounts.

features.title: Event invitations
features.description: Calendar invitations show as a compact card with Accept, Tentative and Decline right in the message, also when someone forwards one to you. The mail list shows the event date before you open it.
